edit.description: refuse at the unresolved-boundary leg in resolveLastRelease

summary: Refuse when CHANGELOG.md records a version whose boundary commit does not resolve, instead of falling through to the semver tag
acceptance: resolveLastRelease reaches the tag fallback only when no version was recorded; a recorded version with no resolvable boundary commit throws and main() exits non-zero naming the version
tests: a recorded CHANGELOG version whose boundary commit does not resolve refuses instead of falling through to the tag
notes: scripts/build-changelog.mjs:86-108 — `if (sha) return sha.trim()` has no else. Reproduced: CHANGELOG.md on disk records 0.9.0, the cut is uncommitted so `git log -S` over the path is empty, and the draft is mined from tag v0.6.2, re-listing an already-released build: commit. Same harm the EISDIR refusal at :78 blocks, by the other door; the module doc at :19-22 already claims absence is the fallback's whole trigger.

edit.description: give the tag-fallback case a subject to exclude

summary: Make the semver-tag-fallback case judge the boundary it names — today it passes with the fallback deleted

per.section: A green verdict is proven non-vacuous

acceptance: the tag-fallback case carries a build: commit before the tag and asserts its absence from the draft, so deleting the fallback reds it
pins: the semver tag fallback excludes a build: commit that predates the tag
notes: tests/build-changelog.test.ts:142 — the fixture's only pre-tag commit is a non-build: seed, so the sole assertion (draft contains AFTER-TAG-FEATURE) holds identically when resolveLastRelease returns null. Verified this tick: output byte-identical with the `tags.length > 0` branch disabled.
